rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tranquil soul is the believer who completed earthly life according to the model of revering God's commands and showing compassion to creation.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın emrine saygı ve Allah’ın yarattıklarına şefkat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafs mutma'inna denotes a believer whose soul matured through a life lived according to that model.
rows.anchor: “imanın huzuruna kavuşmuş insan”, dünya hayatını bu modele göre yaşayıp tamamlamış olan mümindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the person directly without an introductory afterlife formula is a graceful, warm honor that lets the promise of otherworldly happiness reach into this life.
rows.anchor: doğrudan insana hitap edilmesi, Cenâb-ı Hakk’ın bu yapıdaki kullarına çok güzel bir iltifatı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At this station inner conflict, distress, and tension end; the person is at peace with God, other people, and himself.
rows.anchor: Allah ile barışık, insanlarla barışık ve kendisiyle barışıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest happiness is perfect servitude that pleases the Lord, followed by God's reward and the believer's own contentment with Him.
rows.anchor: kulluktaki kemali sayesinde rabbini kendisinden hoşnut etmiş, rabbi tarafından ödüllendirilerek kendisi de O’ndan hoşnut kalmış olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's calling the admitted to Paradise “My servants” is a supreme honor; their final gift is divine pleasure, greater than all other blessings.
rows.anchor: “Benim kullarım” diye anması iltifatların en güzelidir

rows.speaker: Tefsirlerde verilen bilgiler
rows.claim: The verses concern arrogant Meccan leaders who trusted their wealth, thought themselves invincible, and expected to defeat the Prophet.
rows.anchor: malına mülküne güvenerek kendilerini yenilmez zanneden Mekke’nin şımarık ileri gelenleri

rows.speaker: Bazı yorumlar
rows.claim: One interpretation is that some regretted spending so much money in an effort to make the Prophet fail.
rows.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’i başarısız kılma uğruna harcadıkları onca mala üzülüyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows very well the purposes for which such people spend their wealth.
rows.anchor: Yüce Allah’ın böylelerinin hangi maksatlarla mal harcadıklarını gayet iyi bildiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Thamud exemplifies a community's wrong choice after humans were given the ability to choose good or evil; its destruction is a warning, as in the accounts in al-A'raf and Hud.
rows.anchor: Semûd kavminin yanlış seçimi ve bu yüzden başlarına gelen büyük felâket

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel's slaughter alone did not cause the disaster: it was punishment for denying Salih's prophethood, calling him a liar, and persisting in evil.
rows.anchor: felâket, 14. âyette belirtilen “tekzib”in yani Allah’ın elçisi Salih’i peygamber olarak tanımayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is responsible for clarifying the paths of guidance and error, good and evil, by sending scripture and prophets.
rows.anchor: Kitap indirmek ve peygamber göndermek suretiyle hidayet ve dalâlet yollarını, hayrı ve şerri açıklamak Allah’a aittir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since both worldly and afterlife existence belong to God's governance, people should seek the good of both from Him.
rows.anchor: her iki dünyanın kendi yönetiminde olduğunu belirtmekte, dolayısıyla her iki dünyanın iyilik ve güzelliklerini O’ndan istememiz gerektiğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alongside showing people the right path, God warns through revelation and prophets against Hell, the consequence of following the wrong path.
rows.anchor: yanlış yolda gitmenin sonucu olan cehenneme karşı da onları vahiy ve peygamberleri aracılığıyla uyarmıştır

rows.speaker: Birinci yorum
rows.claim: One reading says the Prophet's coming life, especially the later phase of his prophetic mission, will be better and more successful than its beginning.
rows.anchor: bundan sonraki hayatın bundan önceki hayatından daha güzel ve başarılı olacak

rows.speaker: İkinci yorum
rows.claim: Another reading takes the Hereafter's eternal life in Paradise to be better than the temporary life of this world.
rows.anchor: Ebedî olan âhirette cennetteki hayatın geçici olan dünya hayatından daha güzel olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the first reading: against claims that revelation had stopped and Muhammad's cause would fail, God promises his future prophetic work will be spiritually and practically more fruitful.
rows.anchor: bundan sonraki hayatının, peygamberlik faaliyetlerinin ruhanî tekâmülünün öncekinden daha verimli, daha başarılı olacağını müjdelemiştir

rows.speaker: Putperestler
rows.claim: The idolaters said revelation no longer came to Muhammad and God had forgotten him, hoping his mission would end in failure.
rows.anchor: “Artık Muhammed’e vahiy gelmiyor; Allah onu unuttu” gibi sözler söyleyerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad lost his father before birth and his mother at six; his grandfather and then uncle Abu Talib raised him, and Abu Talib defended him despite not openly declaring belief.
rows.anchor: önce dedesi Abdülmuttalib’in, onun ölümünden sonra da amcası Ebû Tâlib’in himayesinde yetişmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abu Talib and Khadija died, the polytheists intensified their attacks; the surah consoles the Prophet by recalling God's past gifts and promising a better future.
rows.anchor: Bu sûrede Allah, o güne kadar peygamberine verdiklerini hatırlatarak teselli etmiş, geleceğinin daha iyi olacağını da müjdelemiştir

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Some say Muhammad got lost as a child in a Meccan valley and God enabled him to find his way back to his grandfather.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah küçükken Mekke vadilerinden birinde yolunu şaşırıp kaybolmuştu

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Others say he became lost on the road to Syria with Abu Talib but found his uncle with God's help.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah amcası Ebû Tâlib’le birlikte Suriye’ye giderken yolda kaybolmuştu

rows.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
rows.claim: The majority reading compares Muhammad's pre- and post-prophetic life: before revelation he saw his society's beliefs and way of life were wrong but did not know how to guide it; the Qur'an showed him both destination and path.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’ı göndererek onu bu durumdan kurtarıp yolunu aydınlattı; ona hem varacağı hedefi hem de o hedefe nasıl varacağını öğretti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can recall that Muhammad escaped poverty through trade, marrying wealthy Khadija, and her entrusting her wealth to him.
rows.anchor: gerek kendisinin ticarî faaliyetleri gerekse zengin bir tüccar olan Hz. Hatice ile evlenmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enrichment may instead mean that revelation made the Prophet spiritually and intellectually rich in truths that could illuminate him and humanity.
rows.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın resulüne gönderdiği vahiy ile onun ruh ve kalp dünyasını zenginleştirmesi

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Some exegetes say recalling this life change assures Muhammad that the God who provided these means would not be displeased with or abandon him.
rows.anchor: kendisine bu imkânları sağlayan Allah’ın ona darılmasının, kendisini terketmesinin söz konusu olamayacağı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because orphans and poor people faced abuse, seizure of their property, and neglect in pre-Islamic society, these commands call society to address two major moral and social problems.
rows.anchor: Onların hakları gözetilmez, malları ellerinden alınır, kendilerine zulmedilirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands also make gratitude for the Prophet's gifts concrete: protect the orphan, guide rather than turn away an inquirer, and help rather than scold a petitioner.
rows.anchor: Allah onu yetim iken korumuştur; o da yetimi incitmemeli, himaye etmelidir

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Some interpret the Lord's blessing as the Qur'an, prophethood, or the specific gifts mentioned in this surah.
rows.anchor: “nimet” kelimesini “Kur’an, peygamberlik, bu sûrede Resûlullah’a lutfedildiği bildirilen şeyler” gibi değişik mânalarla açıklamışlarsa da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the comprehensive sense: all material and spiritual favors the Prophet enjoyed throughout his life, which better fits the surah's purpose and flow.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın hayatı boyunca mazhar olduğu maddî ve mânevî bütün lütuflar, nimetler olarak anlamak sûrenin amacına ve âyetlerin akışına daha uygun düşmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing in the Prophet's biography suggests the warnings were prompted by misconduct; Qur'anic instruction addresses all humanity through him.
rows.anchor: burada onun şahsında bütün insanlığa hitap edilmektedir

rows.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
rows.claim: Raghib explains expansion of the breast as God widening the heart through divine light into peace, calm, and relief.
rows.anchor: kalbin ilâhî bir nur ile Allah tarafından bir huzur ve sükûnet, bir rahatlık ile genişletilmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Considering al-Zumar 39:22, the author finds it suitable to understand this as revelation expanding the Prophet's human capacity for understanding to its fullest.
rows.anchor: beşerî idrak kapasitesinin vahiy ile arttırıldığına ve âzami seviyeye çıkarıldığına işaret olarak anlamak uygun olur

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: Exegetes also explain the expansion as clarity of mind and spiritual elevation given to understand and preserve revelation and fulfill prophethood.
rows.anchor: ona indirilen vahyi anlaması, koruması ve peygamberlik görevini yerine getirebilmesi için kendisine verilmiş olan zihin açıklığı

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Some read the verses as describing the Prophet's spiritual strengthening when revelation resumed after an interval.
rows.anchor: bir süre ara verilmiş olan vahyin yeniden başlamasıyla Hz. Peygamber’in mâneviyatının güçlendirildiğine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden removed may be the Prophet's anguish at his society's faith and morals, quieted or eased when revelation gave him hope and relief.
rows.anchor: arasında yaşadığı topluluğun inanç ve ahlâk yönünden içine düştüğü durumdan dolayı duyduğu ıstırabın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God removed the burden by granting support in establishing monotheism and virtues such as justice, honesty, mercy, and cooperation in good.
rows.anchor: Tevhid inancını ve insan ilişkilerinde adalet, dürüstlük, merhamet, iyilikte yardımlaşma gibi erdemleri hâkim kılma mücadelesinde

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: Exegetes illustrate the Prophet's exalted renown through his mention in sacred books, his name alongside God's in the testimony of faith, reverence from angels and believers, and commands pairing obedience to him with obedience to God.
rows.anchor: kelime-i şehâdette onun isminin Allah’ın ismiyle birlikte yer almasını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being sent as a mercy to all worlds also expresses his exalted renown; the early verse may promise that his name and religion will later spread worldwide.
rows.anchor: ileride Resûlullah’ın isminin ve tebliğ ettiği dinin bütün dünyada tanınıp yayılacağını bildiren bir müjde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recalling human creation, abilities, and gifts, the passage says sound thought should lead to faith and denial has no sound intellectual or evidential basis.
rows.anchor: bütün bu kanıtlara rağmen dini inkâr etmenin ilim ve akıl yönünden sağlam bir dayanağının bulunamayacağı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dīn may also mean the Hereafter and Day of Judgment, which ultimately is a requirement of religion and belief.
rows.anchor: Âyetteki dîn kelimesini “âhiret ve yargı günü” olarak anlamak da mümkündür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's justice governs creation and the universe, gives the truest rulings through prophets in this world, and will judge all creatures most justly in the Hereafter; the question form makes this certain.
rows.anchor: Sözün soru şeklinde olması hükmün kesinliğini gösterir

rows.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
rows.claim: The Prophet advised the reciter to answer that indeed God is the fairest judge and to testify to it.
rows.anchor: Evet, öyledir; ben de buna şahitlik edenlerdenim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These were the first revelation; the command to read addresses Muhammad and all Muslims, and its repetition stresses the importance of reading and knowledge, through which humans are distinguished among living things.
rows.anchor: İlk vahyin “oku” emriyle başlaması ve bu emrin iki defa tekrar edilmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspecified object of reading includes revelation, cosmic signs, and everything to study and understand for lessons and useful results; knowing the Creator is knowledge and religion's chief aim.
rows.anchor: okunması yani üzerinde inceleme yapıp zihin yorarak hakkında bilgi edinilmesi, ders ve ibret alınması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading can mean in the Creator Lord's name or for the Creator; every reading or activity should begin with, serve, and seek help from God rather than another being.
rows.anchor: okumanın (veya herhangi bir faaliyetin) Allah’ın adıyla, Allah için ve Allah adına yapılması emredilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is stressed because God made both human capacity for reading and the objects studied; denying God or gratitude while using these gifts is profound ingratitude.
rows.anchor: bütün bu lütufları görmezlikten gelerek Allah’a şükretmemek, O’nu tanımamak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alaq has dictionary senses including attachment, affection, clotted blood, or a blood-sucking worm; here it is understood as the fertilized ovum attached to the uterine wall, and knowing Creator and creation is necessary for human development.
rows.anchor: aşılanmış yumurtanın ana rahminin iç cidarına asılı vaziyetinin (zigot) kastedildiği anlaşılmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third verse answers Muhammad's indirect statement that he could not read: God's limitless grace can teach through ordinary means or directly without a teacher or learning instrument.
rows.anchor: O, kullarından dilediğine, bir öğretici ve öğrenim aracılığı olmadan bilgi öğretmeye de kadirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen preserves and transmits sciences, wisdom, history, books, and revelation across generations; its functional sense includes all tools of reading, writing, and information exchange through computers.
rows.anchor: bilinen kalemden bilgisayara kadar bütün okuma, yazma ve bilgi alıp verme araçlarını kapsadığını

rows.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the criticized human as Abu Jahl; a report says he vowed to trample Muhammad while praying, but retreated when confronted by a fiery barrier and winged beings, and the Prophet said angels would have seized him; the event occasioned 96:6-19.
rows.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu 6. âyette eleştirilen “insan” ile bilhassa İslâm’ın en azılı düşmanlarından olan Ebû Cehil’in kastedildiğini belirtirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond the occasion, the passage criticizes people in every age who forget God in life's struggle, rely only on themselves, and claim to need no divine help.
rows.anchor: hangi devirde olursa olsun insanın hayat mücadelesinde Allah’ı unutup yalnız kendine güvenmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā is a negative particle indicating that what follows should not happen; here it rebukes arrogant ingratitude, self-sufficiency, and turning from truth.
rows.anchor: kellâ kelimesi olumsuzluk edatı olup devamında kendisinden sonra anlatılanların aslında olmaması gerektiğini ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are weak and depend on God and society; God owns and can remove all resources, so boasting, disobedience, superiority, and claiming control of one's fate reflect ignorance, weak faith, and lack of insight.
rows.anchor: İnsanların ellerinde bulunan bütün imkânların gerçek sahibi ise kendileri değil

rows.speaker: Bu görüşü benimseyenler
rows.claim: Those who regard al-Alaq as the first surah consider this the Qur'an's first verse to point to the Hereafter: worldly life is temporary, all return for judgment, and people should prepare and avoid transgression; later verses make the afterlife and accountability explicit.
rows.anchor: bu âyet de Kur’an’da âhiret hayatına dikkat çekmek üzere inmiş ilk âyet olup bir uyarı olarak dünya hayatının geçiciliğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's translation links this verse to the prior two: it warns those who treat possessions as their own, forget God is their true owner, and become arrogant and transgress.
rows.anchor: elindekini kendine ait sanan, Allah’ın gerçek sahip ve mâlik olduğu bilincinden yoksun bulunan, bu yüzden böbürlenen

rows.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
rows.claim: Most exegetes take these verses as a rebuke to Abu Jahl for trying to stop Muhammad and believers from praying at the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’e hitap ederek onun ve müminlerin Kâbe önünde namaz kılmalarını engellemeye kalkışan Ebû Cehil’e karşı bir eleştiri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A universal reading is more suitable: all tyrants in every age who obstruct religion's work of shaping social life by goodness, truth, and justice are criticized.
rows.anchor: her dönemde görülen ve dinin sosyal hayatı iyilik, hak ve adalet ilkeleri yönünde şekillendirme işlevini engellemek isteyen bütün zorbaların eleştirildiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is unjust to stop someone who is rightly guided and urges others to reverence God and act responsibly from worship or religious duties.
rows.anchor: doğru yolda olan hem de başkalarına Allah’a saygılı olmayı ve sorumluluk şuuru içerisinde bulunmayı emreden bir kimsenin

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: Seizing the forelock is figurative; explanations include taking the offender to Hell, disgracing him, stamping his forehead, or humiliating him.
rows.anchor: “Onu tutup cehenneme atacağız, yüzünü kara çıkaracağız, alnını damgalayacağız, alçaltacağız” gibi değişik şekillerde açıklanmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A self-satisfied tyrant who blocks worship may be left free for a time, but will ultimately be caught and punished in this world, the Hereafter, or both; Abu Jahl and others suffered defeat here and will face the promised afterlife punishment.
rows.anchor: sonunda bir gün gelip yakasına yapışılacağı, hak ettiği cezayı göreceği bildirilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nādī derives from consultation and means the council assembled for deliberation; Meccan consultation meetings took place at Dār al-Nadwa.
rows.anchor: “bir konuda istişare etmek üzere toplanmak” anlamına gelen nedve kökünden türemiş olup kurultayda bir araya gelen heyeti ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabāniya is a plural from a root meaning to push or drive away and, as a religious term, means angels of punishment.
rows.anchor: “itmek, savmak” anlamına gelen zeben kelimesinden türemiş çoğul bir isim olup dinî terim olarak azap meleklerini ifade eder

rows.speaker: Rivayete göre
rows.claim: After Abu Jahl threatened Muhammad while he prayed at Abraham's station and boasted of his many supporters, the verses challenged him to call his council while God would call the angels of punishment; he never dared act despite hearing them.
rows.anchor: Allah Teâlâ, “O hemen kurultayını çağırsın, biz de zebânileri çağıracağız” buyurarak Hz. Peygamber’e meydan okuyan Ebû Cehil’in yetersizliğini ortaya koymak istemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated kallā indicates the tyrant will not dare summon supporters; Muhammad must not obey him but continue prayer and prostration, through which a servant draws nearest to God, as the Prophet taught.
rows.anchor: namaz kılmaya ve secde etmeye devam ederek Allah’a yakınlaşma gayretlerini sürdürmesi emredilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadr can mean power, decree, value, or honor; the night is named for the honor the Qur'an's descent gave it. Duhan calls it blessed, while al-Baqara places the Qur'an's descent in Ramadan, so the night falls within that month.
rows.anchor: Kadr kelimesi sözlükte “güç, hüküm, değer, şeref” gibi anlamlara gelir

rows.speaker: Hz. Âişe’ye isnad edilen hadis
rows.claim: A hadith identifying the first revelation with Ramadan's twenty-seventh night contributed to the general view that Laylat al-Qadr is the twenty-seventh; other reports place the beginning of revelation in the last ten days.
rows.anchor: Kadir gecesinin Ramazan’ın 27. gecesi olduğu yönünde genel bir kanaat oluşmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is not identified precisely, a choice explained in part as preventing people from relying on its reward and neglecting worship at other times.
rows.anchor: Kadir gecesinin kesin olarak bildirilmemesi, insanların o gecede kazanacakları sevaplara güvenip diğer zamanlarda kulluk görevlerini ihmal etmelerini önlemek

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: Exegetes agree that the pronoun “it” refers to the Qur'an; its name is omitted because it is so well known and exalted.
rows.anchor: Müfessirler, “Biz onu Kadir gecesinde indirdik” diye çevirdiğimiz 1. âyetteki “o” zamiriyle Kur’an’ın kastedildiği konusunda ittifak etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Âlimlerin çoğu
rows.claim: Most scholars infer from enzelnā rather than the gradual-revelation verb nezzelnā that the whole Qur'an descended from the divine realm to the lowest heaven.
rows.anchor: peyderpey indirdik” anlamındaki nezzelnâ yerine “indirdik” anlamındaki enzelnâ fiilinin kullanılmasını gerekçe göstererek

rows.speaker: Bazı âlimler
rows.claim: Some scholars instead understand the verse to refer directly to the first verses of al-Alaq revealed to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: doğrudan Hz. Peygamber’e gelen Alak sûresinin ilk âyetlerinin kastedildiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than date the night, the following verses answer the question by stressing its importance and blessing; Duhan also says wise matters are apportioned on that blessed night.
rows.anchor: onun tarihinin açıklanması yerine bu gecenin önemi, insanlar için hayır ve bereketi üzerinde durulmuştur

rows.speaker: Müfessirlerin bir kısmı
rows.claim: Some take a thousand months literally: worship and good works that night earn more reward than a thousand months without it.
rows.anchor: bu gecede yapılan ibadet ve hayırların, içinde Kadir gecesinin bulunmadığı bin ayda yapılanlardan daha çok sevap getireceğini

rows.speaker: Başka bir yorum
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes a thousand as a figure for great abundance: worship and good deeds that night surpass those done at all other times.
rows.anchor: bin sayısı çokluktan kinayedir

rows.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the Spirit as Gabriel, who is separately named to show his exalted rank; the Qur'an elsewhere identifies him as the Spirit (26:193-194).
rows.anchor: 4. âyetteki “ruh”tan maksat Cebrâil’dir

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Others take the Spirit to mean leading angels, an unseen army other than angels, or mercy.
rows.anchor: Ruha “meleklerin ileri gelenleri, meleklerin dışında Allah’ın görünmez ordularından bir ordu, rahmet” vb. mânalar verenler de vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels and the Spirit descend with assignments from God; in groups they greet believers from the start of night until dawn, making it a night of peace and happiness.
rows.anchor: melekler gecenin başından itibaren şafak sökünceye kadar gruplar halinde inerek müminlere selâm verirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God manifests through the name al-Rahman on this night, sustaining general peace, order, and balance for at least a year, as inferred from Duhan 44:4-6.
rows.anchor: düzeni ve dengeyi korumaktadır

rows.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
rows.claim: The Prophet withdrew for retreat in the mosque during Ramadan's final ten days, spending his time chiefly in worship and reflection.
rows.anchor: vaktini daha çok ibadet ve tefekkürle geçirirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should revive Laylat al-Qadr with worship and prayer; when Aisha asked how, the Prophet recommended asking God, the forgiving one who loves forgiveness, to forgive her.
rows.anchor: Allahım! Sen affedicisin, affı seversin, beni affet! de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laylat al-Qadr is one of the blessed nights later known as kandil nights and the most important among them, observed through worship and ceremonies in Islamic culture.
rows.anchor: “kandil geceleri” denilen ve zamanla İslâm kültür tarihinde kutlu olduğuna inanılıp çeşitli ibadetlerle ihya edilen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book here especially means Jews and Christians around Medina, and polytheists means the pagan Arabs; though local groups are named, the ruling concerns all humanity.
rows.anchor: yahudilerle hıristiyanlar; “müşrikler”den maksat ise dönemin putperest Araplar’ıdır

rows.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
rows.claim: Most exegetes say Jews, Christians, and pagans would not abandon disbelief until a clear proof, namely a prophet, came to them.
rows.anchor: kendilerine açık kanıt yani peygamber gelinceye kadar içinde bulundukları inkârcılıktan ayrılıp ona son vermeyeceklerdir

rows.speaker: Diğer bir yorum
rows.claim: Another reading says God would not let the People of the Book and polytheists addressed by Muhammad die before sending them a new divine message at the appointed time.
rows.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in muhatapları olan Ehl-i kitap ile müşrikleri, –yeni bir ilâhî mesajın zamanı geldiği için– o mesajı göndermeden dünyadan ayırmayacaktır

rows.speaker: Üçüncü yorum
rows.claim: A third reading says these groups would not be punished until messenger and proof had been sent to them.
rows.anchor: kendilerine elçi ve kanıt gelmedikçe, gönderilmedikçe cezalandırılmayacakları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the third reading more contextually fitting: despite human capacities to distinguish right from wrong, divine mercy means those not reached by clear proof and the message are not punished, as stated at 17:15.
rows.anchor: açık kanıt göndermediği ve mesajının ulaşmadığı kimseleri yaptıklarından dolayı cezalandırmayacağını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proof named in verse 1 is Muhammad, sent to recite the Qur'an's pure pages, free of lies, hypocrisy, doubt, error, and deviation.
rows.anchor: “tertemiz sayfalar” ise Kur’an’ın sayfaları olup “tertemiz” nitelemesi, “yalan, nifak, şüphe, sapkınlık ve yanlışlık vb. kusurlardan arınmış sayfalar”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The books in those pages are upright divine verses and rulings distinguishing truth from falsehood; the Qur'an may be so described because it includes earlier scriptures' rulings.
rows.anchor: dosdoğru, hakkı bâtıldan ayıran ilâhî âyetler ve hükümler bulunduğunu bildirmektedir

rows.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the clear proof as Muhammad, whose message and miracles made him a manifest messenger of truth; the People of the Book are blamed for disagreeing about him, after having agreed a final prophet would come, since most rejected him while some believed.
rows.anchor: son peygamberin geleceği hakkında fikir birliği içerisinde bulunduğunu, fakat Hz. Peygamber geldikten sonra bir kısmı ona inandığı, çoğu ise inkâr ettiği

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur takes the clear proof as Jesus: although earlier prophets foretold him and he was sent to Israel, most rejected his prophethood, dividing into Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: bu âyetteki “açık kanıt”la Hz. Îsâ’nın gelişi kastedilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author renders “making religion sincere for God” as believing in and obeying God wholeheartedly; worship's essential spirit is intention, sincerity, monotheism, and awareness of servitude, while its forms remain necessary.
rows.anchor: ibadetin özü ve ruhu niyet ve ihlâstır, tevhid inancı ve kulluk bilincidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanif primarily means monotheism: turning from every deviant view tainted by associating partners and worshipping God alone with sincerity.
rows.anchor: Şirk kuşkusu taşıyan her türlü sapkın görüşten uzaklaşıp Allah’ın birliği inancına yönelen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and almsgiving are separately named because they are especially valuable: prayer expresses reverence for God and zakat compassion for people; these duties belong to the revealed upright religion and existed in uncorrupted earlier faiths.
rows.anchor: Namaz Allah’a saygının, zekât ise insana şefkat ve sevginin en anlamlı ifadeleridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinan Jews and Christians knew of Muhammad's mission yet rejected him and the Qur'an, while pagans associated partners with God; the call to worship, pray, and give zakat invites them to Islam.
rows.anchor: son peygamber Hz. Muhammed’in risâleti hakkında bilgi sahibi oldukları halde, o hak peygamberi ve Kur’an’ı inkâr ettikleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers merit punishment as the worst of creation, while believers who do good merit bliss as the best; their greatest happiness is God's approval and an indescribably beautiful reward, and they are filled with contentment toward Him because they fear their Lord.
rows.anchor: onlara gözlerin görmediği, kulakların işitmediği ve insan aklının tasavvur edemeyeceği derecede güzel bir ödül hazırlanmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first trumpet blast will cause earth-shaking quakes and mountains to scatter, destroying all standing structures; the terror of the Day of Resurrection calls people to prepare.
rows.anchor: yerküresinde şiddetli sarsıntılar meydana gelecek ve dağlar yerlerinden kopup savrulacak

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: The earth casting out its burdens is explained as resurrected dead leaving their graves or as underground minerals, gases, and lava emerging; exegetes place it with the second trumpet blast.
rows.anchor: Kabirlerdeki ölülerin dirilip dışarı çıkması

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: A second explanation of the earth's burdens is the emergence of underground minerals, gases, and lava.
rows.anchor: Yer altındaki madenler, gazlar, ve lâvların dışarı çıkması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing unprecedented convulsions, people express fear and astonishment by asking what is happening to the earth.
rows.anchor: daha önce bu derecede şiddetli bir sarsıntı görülmemiştir

rows.speaker: Birinci yorum
rows.claim: One interpretation says God gives the earth a kind of speech so it openly reports what happened on it and who acted; a hadith says the earth will speak at resurrection.
rows.anchor: Allah yere bir çeşit konuşma ve anlatma yeteneği verir

rows.speaker: İkinci yorum
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the earth, by God's decree, itemizes everything people did upon it.
rows.anchor: arz, üstünde olup bitenleri tek tek sayıp dökercesine insanların orada yaptıkları her şeyi açığa çıkarır

rows.speaker: Üçüncü yorum
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes the earth's speech as its announcement that the world has ended and the Hereafter has arrived.
rows.anchor: dünyanın son bulduğunu ve âhiretin geldiğini haber verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether the earth literally speaks is less important than making the end of worldly life and everyone's deeds plain; people should live so it testifies good things about them.
rows.anchor: insanların bu gerçeği göz önüne alarak o gün arzın kendisi hakkında iyi şeyler söylemesini sağlayacak bir hayat yaşamalarıdır

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: People emerging in groups may appear in good or bad condition according to their deeds, or travel in groups from different regions; the author allows that all these meanings may apply.
rows.anchor: Herkesin kabirlerinden çıkıp mahşer yerine doğru ilerlerken dünyadaki amellerine göre iyi veya kötü şartlar altında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person's worldly choices, faith, and conduct determine their Hereafter and whether they join the good or bad, establishing nontransferable individual responsibility from the moment of emergence.
rows.anchor: her bir insanın âhiretteki durumunu, âkıbetini, iyiler arasında mı yoksa kötüler arasında mı olacağını belirleyen şeyin, bizzat kendisinin bu dünyadaki tercihi

rows.speaker: Tefsirlerde
rows.claim: The phrase about being shown one's deeds is explained either as seeing the records in the book of deeds or as seeing the reward or punishment for what one did.
rows.anchor: Amel defterlerindeki kayıtları görmeleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These concise, comprehensive verses state that every person ultimately faces the result of their deeds; the Prophet called them an unmatched concise expression and urged protection from the Fire even through half a date or a good word.
rows.anchor: dünyada yapılan en küçük hayır veya şerrin bile kaybolmayacağını

rows.speaker: Birinci yorum
rows.claim: To reconcile this promise with verses saying unbelievers' good deeds do not benefit them in the Hereafter, one explanation is that unbelievers receive the reward for good deeds in this world.
rows.anchor: İnançsızlar yaptıkları iyiliklerin karşılığını dünyada görürler

rows.speaker: İkinci yorum
rows.claim: Another explanation is that both believers and unbelievers see their deeds, but God forgives believers' sins and rewards their good works; unbelievers' good deeds are rejected for lacking God's purpose, leaving only sins.
rows.anchor: Mümine de inkârcıya da yaptıkları gösterilir; Allah müminin günahlarını bağışlar

rows.speaker: Üçüncü yorum
rows.claim: A third view says unbelievers' deeds are assessed and their greatest sin of disbelief is offset by no good deed, so their good works are fruitless in this respect.
rows.anchor: inkârına ait büyük günahından düşülür ama iyilikleri bu günahı karşılayamaz

rows.speaker: İslâm âlimlerinin genel kabulüne göre
rows.claim: Though theologians offer explanations, God alone knows the reality of the Hereafter and its events and determines each servant's ultimate fate according to justice and wisdom.
rows.anchor: âhiret âleminin ve orada olup biteceklerin hakikat ve mahiyetini Allah Teâlâ bilir
